status: post-hoc exploratory extension, not a replacement for frozen H1-H4
reason: Fold pooling suppresses between-person attribution variability.
ranking: For each outer fold, take the median and unscaled MAD across the 42 normalised out-of-fold person vectors; score = median - lambda * MAD.
lambda_selection: None. Report every candidate; do not select using outer scores.
model: Same XGBoost and 200000-window stratified training budget as original P3
comparison: Within each participant compare against original fold-aggregated ranking at the same lambda and k.
reuse: Only exact same participant, channel set, training budget, seed and model protocol. Record source row for each reuse.
inference: 43 paired participant scores; 10000-resample percentile bootstrap. Wilcoxon and Holm over all 60 reduced-size comparisons, labelled exploratory.
non_inferiority: All margins 0.01, 0.02, 0.03 versus matching k16 reference; report unadjusted LCB and Holm within each lambda and margin.
limitations: Attribution windows retain the original random sampling. Equal weight across people does not imply class-balanced attribution or repeated inner model fits. The 42 vectors share five fitted models; their MAD is descriptive heterogeneity, not a sampling standard error.
